messages.subject: comparison and boolean operators, conditional and while statements
parts:
I just pushed a finished version of boolean
operators (binary &&, ||, unary !), comparison
operators (<, <=, >, >=, ==, !=), conditional
statements (if, else if, else), and loop statements
(while). They all have the same syntax (including
precedence and associativity) and semantics as in C++.

So far, nothing is vectorized, so the boolean operators and
conditionals only apply to primitive int or real types.
As in C++ (and in R, I just checked), non-zero values
are "true" and zero values "false". So the conditionals
and while loops

I wrote general template metaprograms to vectorize
unary and binary ops. There's really no efficiency gain
here over just writing the loops in Stan, so I haven't
put it in yet. After more thought, I've come to agree
with Marcus that it's least confusing if we just allow
either exactly matching type or scalar arguments. That is,
no broadcasting 1D arrays to 2D arrays or vectors to matrices.
If we want that, we can go with an explicit syntax like Eigen's.

- Bob
